correctness.rationale: Universal proof: when at most six goods, each first turn precedes every second turn. For every ordered envy pair, the first-turn deviation to the later of the recipient’s at-most-two goods is feasible and guarantees its singleton utility by monotonicity, so Nash optimality implies EF1. Seven-good existence: the exact additive payoff matrix, all 128 continuation states and 448 actions, and independently 13700 ordered histories, are checked against a complete standalone dynamic-programming certificate with explicit tie resolution. The root allocation fails EF1 strictly for B towards A (1120 versus minimum residual 1286), and distinct bundles have distinct valuations.

value.rationale: An exact, sharp minimal-goods boundary for the loss of equilibrium EF1 in online round-robin is a natural structural invariant of strategic fair division. It improves the only directly located online example from nine to seven goods and supplies a universally valid six-good safety proof. The witness uses strictly positive generic additive valuations, making it a reusable rigorous test case and a meaningful online-versus-offline equilibrium distinction.
